summary: Dedicated capacity GPU OOM eviction caused embeddings truncation and SLA exposure for Northfold Financial (post-incident follow-up)
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-02-23 at ~12:14 UTC Northfold Financial observed truncated embedding responses (lengths far shorter than expected) and a spike in 5xx errors for requests routed to their Dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1. This coincided with a sharp billing delta reported by the customer and active customer escalation to Support + CSM.

Impact:
- Customer-facing embeddings returned truncated vectors for ~14 minutes for ~8% of requests during the window.
- Several downstream ranking tasks degraded leading to visible product regressions for Northfold's customers.
- Billing meter showed a transient spike due to repeated retries and request replay behavior from the customer side.
- SLA exposure: several requests exceeded latency SLOs; customer flagged as enterprise and requested urgent remediation and credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-east-1.
- Models: redwood-embed-compact-v1 pinned in customer config.
- Autoscaler set to conservative scale-up (min 2, max 6 GPU workers).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send batch embedding request set used in production (payloads ~2k tokens per request).
2) Observe intermittent truncated embeddings and 5xx responses logged by the client.
3) Replaying requests sometimes returned success after a retry.

Raw error snippets / logs:
- "runtime: eviction due to OOM: host node oom-kill, worker pid 11234 exit code 137" (serving-runtime logs).
- SRE dashboard: GPU memory pressure spiked to ~98% on host gpu-03c for the pool; kernel swap activity observed.
- Autoscaler logs: scaling action delayed by 67s due to coordinator contention.

Customer communication template used:
- Initial acknowledgement within 6 minutes. Provided incident short summary and time window.
- CSM called customer within 20 minutes and offered active monitoring and credits pending root cause.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-02-23 12:20 UTC): Acknowledged customer. Opened incident INC-2026-02-23-01 and escalated to SRE. Customer reports truncated 768-d embeddings returned as length ~64 for a subset of calls.

Ravi Patel (2026-02-23 12:32 UTC): Initial triage: observed host-level OOMs on gpu-03c in dedicated pool -> container PID 11234 killed. Marking as suspected GPU memory regression on kernel selection for redwood-embed-compact-v1.

Alex Gomez (SRE) (2026-02-23 12:47 UTC): Confirmed eviction events consistent with memory leak pattern: memory climbed steadily across the previous hour. Live heap traces requested from runtime team. Pinpointed most failures to a single host; started mitigation by draining host.

Priya Singh (Customer Success) (2026-02-23 13:05 UTC): Customer indicates business impact on live ranking pipeline. Offering billing credit and prioritized follow-up. Requested postmortem and timeline for permanent fix.

Ravi Patel (2026-02-23 13:28 UTC): Mitigation: removed gpu-03c from pool, forced rolling restart of worker set, and temporarily increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the pool. Error rate dropped and truncation stopped at ~12:38 UTC.
Maya Chen (2026-02-25 09:15 UTC): Postmortem draft shared with customer; customer requested clarification on root cause around kernel selection/quantization path. Scheduled tech review on 2026-02-26.
Ravi Patel (2026-02-26 16:02 UTC): Patch merged to adjust kalloc heuristic and avoid a pathological allocation pattern (PR reference attached). Follow-up items tracked in CON-411.
investigation_notes:
12:16-12:25 UTC: Correlated customer traces with serving-runtime telemetry; 137 exit codes across two containers on host gpu-03c. Memory footprint increased with request sequence length.
12:30 UTC: Heap dump analysis (runtime team): rapid growth in KV cache retention for prefix keys during long embedding batches; appears to retain per-request tensors when quantized execution path triggers a fallback allocator.
12:40 UTC: Autoscaler logs show scale decision stalled due to scheduler lock contention (thread stack trace attached in internal ticket). The delay allowed memory pressure to reach eviction thresholds on the single affected host.
12:55 UTC: Observability team: discovered a mismatch between runtime's kernel-selection table and the new compact-embed quantization profile shipped in last week's rollout (release v1.14.2). The mismatch caused a fallback to a less memory-efficient kernel under specific shape/seq-length combos.
Hypothesis: Combined effect of (1) quantization-profile mismatch -> increased per-request GPU memory, (2) autoscaler delay -> slower pool growth, and (3) noisy neighbor on gpu-03c -> host OOM and evictions.
Evidence: PRs and release notes correlate: release v1.14.2 included compact-embed profile updates (PR #2890) merged 3 days prior. Host-specific logs show elevated memory for requests routed to gpu-03c vs gpu-03a/b.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation timeline: 12:34 UTC drained gpu-03c and restarted worker set -> immediate reduction in 5xx and truncation. 12:45 UTC autoscaler temporarily set to aggressive scaling (min 3 -> 5) for the pool until patch applied. Incident window considered closed at 12:38 UTC for customer-visible failures.
Permanent fix: Reverted the problematic kernel-selection fallback path in serving-runtime and updated the quantization profile mapping to ensure memory-efficient kernels are selected for compact embeddings. Patch merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2987 (merged 2026-02-25).
SRE changes: Added a guard in dedicated-manager to avoid draining being delayed by scheduler locks; added an alert for 'autoscaler decision > 30s' which will create INT tickets automatically.
Customer remediation: Applied a goodwill credit for the affected billing window (one hour pro-rated) and offered a private postmortem review with engineers. Customer accepted credit and follow-up review scheduled.
Follow-up action items (tracked in CON-411):
- SEV-A: Backfill unit/integration test coverage for new quant profile -> owner: Priya R. -> due 2026-03-10.
- SEV-B: Improve autoscaler contention metrics & add circuit-breaker -> owner: Alex G. -> due 2026-03-05.
- SEV-C: Run dedicated pool soak test for compact-embed profile at scale -> owner: Ravi P. -> due 2026-03-08.
Customer communication notes: Drafted and shared detailed timeline and root cause (2026-02-25). Customer replied 'thank you for the fast response, please share post-fix soak results' and requested a follow-up call on 2026-03-02.
Closure: Incident marked Resolved after patch rolled to prod and soak results for 48h showed no recurrence (2026-02-26).
